analyst_view.overall: Early view: Tenerife play Ceuta first in their emotional return after the death of Jesús de Miguel, so this view will be revisited. They had drawn four in a row under Álvaro Cervera before the tragedy, and Mallorca are also draw-prone (four draws in 12), with their own postponed game at Andorra still to be given a new date.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.0 goals and I lean lower still: Mallorca's last three away league games ended 1-1, 1-1 and 0-0, and Tenerife's run before the tragedy was four draws in a row, three of them 1-1. Adrián Fuentes is the one player who can break a tight game open.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners and I keep it. Neither team has been dominant in recent weeks and both have been content to take draws, so there is no sign of a lopsided game that would push the count up.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards. Mallorca's 3.5 looks a little high for the away side, but with no referee named and Tenerife's mood after the Ceuta game unknown, I hold at the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.0 shots, a low figure that fits two cautious sides. I see nothing yet to move it; Tenerife's first game back against Ceuta will say more about their attacking intent.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 6.6 shots on target. I lean slightly lower in line with the goals: Mallorca's away games have been short of clear chances (a 0-0 at Girona and two 1-1s), and Tenerife lean heavily on Enric Gallego's eight goals.
